timing.label: Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: A plugin is one more supply chain to secure. Why should I let it run in every session?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: Why not just hand each brand team a playbook and skip the packaging?

problem.quote: So I started with the manifest, plugin.json

approach.quote: The plugin has the release skill and the incident skill, plus the rule, the hook, the subagent and the MCP

evidence.quote: I uploaded the full folder again and it was fine

next_step.quote: Basically it's ready for the organization

tag_question_examples: It's easier for everyone in the long run, that's the point, right?

must_mention.point: One plugin ships both procedures as skills together with the freeze rule, the push guard hook, the reviewer subagent and the incident MCP
must_mention.evidence_quote: The plugin has the release skill and the incident skill, plus the rule, the hook, the subagent and the MCP, all in one plugin

must_mention.point: Repository installs follow the branch unless pinned to a SHA, uploads stay pinned to what was uploaded, and a skills-only repo needs no manifest
must_mention.evidence_quote: Repo installs follow the branch unless you pin a SHA, uploads are fixed, and the Lumen repo works without a manifest

must_mention.point: A new uploaded revision replaces the whole bundle, so a partial zip removes every file it left out
The MCP credential is connected after install through a secret reference and never written into the plugin files
must_mention.evidence_quote: you connect the credential after install, it's not written into the plugin files

must_mention.point: Engineers without edit rights can only propose; an admin approves the diff before the shared plugin changes

article_plural_slips: "some files were not there" — say how many: "six files were removed"
sentences_to_rerecord: So I started with the manifest, plugin.json, and basically the name has to be lowercase…
It's easier for everyone in the long run, that's the point, right?

accuracy.anchor: Three of five points; the revision surprise was described without saying a revision replaces the bundle, and the proposal flow was missing. (anchors: 27–30 every point with a file or scope named; 15–20 three of five; under 10 one point)

structure.anchor: Framing opened with the manifest before the outcome; the update had no provenance, guarantee or ask headings. (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only)

customer_relevance.anchor: Named the hook and the token location; no brand-team or checklist number. (anchors: 16–20 reviewer's questions answered with files, scopes and counts; 10–13 some; under 6 feature talk)

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Framing, checkpoint-70 and objection-2 over, update under; six fillers and a 12 s pause. (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off)

recovery.anchor: Objection 1 called the hook a guarantee (capped at 5); objection 2 had a boundary but no number (capped at 4). (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern)

stems: "Every brand team gets…" — first sentence of the framing, before any file name.
"A new revision replaces…" — say what the partial zip removed, with the count.
"The hook is not a guarantee because…" — name where it runs before the reviewer asks.
